children: Benchmark indices held on to most of their opening gains by midday on Wednesday, with the Sensex trading at 81,961.89, up 855.24 points or 1.05 per cent, and the Nifty 50 at 25,270.25, up 225.60 points or 0.90 per cent, as of 1.11 PM. Markets had opened sharply higher after the Diwali holiday, with the Nifty gap-opening near 25,338 and Bank Nifty near 60,525, before trimming some gains through the morning session.

Broad market participation remained strong. Of the 4,586 stocks traded on the BSE, 2,959 advanced against 1,389 declines, with 238 unchanged. As many as 126 stocks hit fresh 52-week highs versus 46 at 52-week lows, while 199 stocks were locked in upper circuits and 163 in lower circuits. The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies stood at ₹5,11,48,794 crore, equivalent to $5.45 trillion.

Mahindra & Mahindra was the top Nifty 50 gainer, rising 4.38 per cent to ₹3,434.80, with volumes of 34.94 lakh shares valued at ₹1,192.19 crore, the highest value traded among gainers. IndiGo was second, up 4.30 per cent to ₹5,663.50, with ₹899.14 crore changing hands. Trent gained 3.55 per cent to ₹3,230.00, Eicher Motors rose 2.58 per cent to ₹7,826.00, and Axis Bank advanced 2.33 per cent to ₹1,341.20.

On the losing side, ICICI Bank was the heaviest by value, falling 1.24 per cent to ₹1,569.30 on volumes of 201.53 lakh shares worth ₹3,221.18 crore. Nestlé India declined 1.22 per cent to ₹1,282.00, Tech Mahindra fell 1.21 per cent to ₹1,783.20, TCS shed 0.74 per cent to ₹2,457.20, and Apollo Hospitals eased 0.68 per cent to ₹8,491.00. The IT sector’s underperformance reflects continued pressure from the prospect of higher US interest rates following Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected inflation data.

“Indian equity markets opened sharply higher, extending the recent bullish momentum, with broad-based buying interest across sectors. Banking and financial stocks led the gains, alongside the auto sector,” said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. He cautioned that “elevated levels and overbought technical conditions could leave room for intermittent bouts of profit-booking at higher levels,” with the Nifty RSI hovering near 80.

On the commodity front, WTI crude was trading near $86.65, up 0.25 per cent, after falling sharply over the past two sessions. Brent briefly fell below $90 on Tuesday for the first time since August following US President Donald Trump’s remarks that the Iran conflict could end soon, before recovering slightly. MCX crude was at ₹8,140, up 0.5 per cent, though the technical bias remains weak. “Cheaper crude is a relief for India’s import bill and the rupee,” Ponmudi noted, adding that a decisive break below ₹8,100 on MCX crude risks a slide to ₹7,800.

Precious metals staged a partial recovery. COMEX gold was at $4,055, up 0.65 per cent, after falling nearly 3 per cent on Tuesday on the hot US CPI print, while COMEX silver outperformed at $52.45, up 2.4 per cent, supported by industrial demand and bargain-hunting. MCX gold rose 0.7 per cent to ₹1,41,480, and MCX silver gained 1.8 per cent to ₹1,85,900. “Tuesday’s large bearish candle engulfed Monday’s gains,” Ponmudi observed, adding that a reclaim above $4,100 on COMEX gold is needed to stabilise the outlook, while a break below $4,000 risks a slide to $3,900.

The Indian rupee continued to hold near recent highs, with USD/INR trading around 93.85, down 0.07 per cent on the day, despite renewed dollar strength after Tuesday’s US inflation data. “The domestic currency continues to draw support from strong foreign portfolio inflows and softer crude oil prices that helped drive its strongest weekly advance of 2026 last week,” Ponmudi said, noting the rupee had appreciated approximately 1.2 per cent last week to reach its highest level since April. The near-term bias for USD/INR remains bearish, with a sustained move above 94 needed to signal stabilisation.
Bank Nifty’s immediate resistance lies at 61,000–61,500, with support at 60,000–59,800, while Nifty support is pegged at 25,200–25,150, followed by 25,000.

title: Indices hold gains at noon; M&M, IndiGo top Nifty charts as IT stocks drag
